item.description: 🤯 Thursday in Europe brings an 'unusual' red card and screamer; watch This Thursday (22) brings Europa League and Conference League action. And two moments in particular caught the eye during the league-phase matches in the two competitions. Check out what happened below. Forgot there's VAR, keeper? France's undisputed first-choice goalkeeper, Maignan left his Milan side a man down 28 minutes into their Europa League clash with Bournemouth. As Justin Kluivert took a corner, he struck Tyler Adams in the face, probably while trying to push the American away. VAR reviewed the incident, and the Rossoneri goalkeeper was shown a red card on English soil. Kluivert had already put Bournemouth ahead from the penalty spot (7'). And things got worse for Milan when Marcus Tavernier also scored a penalty (32'). 🔥 He's FLYING! German striker Paris Brunner has been the standout player for Filipe Luís's Monaco in 2026/2027. He reached ten goals in 12 games this season after brushing aside Freiburg's defending in their Conference League clash. Check out this masterpiece from the 20-year-old at the Stade Louis II: A goal that has Monaco on course for victory. A product of Dortmund's academy, Brunner made just seven appearances (without scoring) for the principality club last season. And he started 26/27 looking like "a different player". He has represented Germany at every youth level — winning the Under-17 European Championship and World Cup in 2023 — and is still seeking his first senior call-up. He is also on the Democratic Republic of the Congo's radar thanks to his family roots. Is Jürgen Klopp keeping an eye on him? This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. Texas' Arch Manning doesn't rank in the top 10 in the SEC, having thrown 11 touchdown passes with five interceptions. Losing Simmons is a lethal blow to this 4-2 Texas team, which hopes to stop the bleeding after its first two-game losing streak since 2021. The Longhorns are in a world of hurt with the absence of consensus five-star recruit Wesley, who has seven tackles and six quarterback pressures this season, and the questionable status of running back Hollywood Smothers. "He's totally dialed," Longhorn defensive lineman Hero Kanu said of Wesley on Monday before his injury was disclosed. "I think physically he's ahead of his time. He's still young, but physically he's so developed. I think he can go out there and make an impact as well." All-America left tackle Trevor Goosby gushed as well, saying, "He has more moves in the bag than your normal edge rusher." Jackson is a very good player but missed six tackles against Florida and is hardly a speed rusher on the edge. Neither is Umeozulu the threat on the perimeter to make life miserable for Chambliss. Biles figures to blitz often even though Will Muschamp's defense blitzes less than any SEC team besides Missouri with a rate of only 16%. The extra problem is Chambliss is incredibly impactful against the blitz. The senior, who led the Rebels to last year's College Football Playoff semifinals, doesn't run often but moves well in the pocket to find open receivers and has completed 62.7% of his throws against the blitz for 608 yards and six touchdowns. Mississippi quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) scrambles as he looks for an open wide receiver during the first half of an NCAA college football game against Missouri, Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026, in Oxford, Miss. (Rogelio V. Solis/AP Photo/Rogelio V. Solis) Sarkisian knows what he's dealing with because Chambliss will be the best quarterback he's faced all season, with apologies to Ohio State's Julian Sayin, who has the luxury of the best receiver in the nation in Jeremiah Smith. Ole Miss is not devoid of talent at receiver with Duce Robinson and Caleb Cunningham. "He's pretty hard to get on the ground," Sarkisian said of Chambliss. "He's a dynamic playmaker, and it's not always about him scrambling to run. It's him scrambling to buy time to create the second play in the passing game, the explosive plays down the field. So I think it's really important thaty we have really good rush lanes, that we try to contain him in the pocket. But he's going to get out." Sarkisian promises he's focused solely on trying to beat Ole Miss even though he is fully aware that a third loss would almost certainly eliminate Texas from the College Football Playoff race. No 9-3 team has earned an at-large berth in the 12-team field. "I think from an energy standpoint, we need to pour into this game," Sarkisian said. "We need to go 1-0 this week. I've never seen the SEC look like this where every team's got a conference loss this early in the year." Not since 2007 has the SEC not had an unbeaten team this early in a season. That notwithstanding, Texas' offense has been so impotent, especially in the running attack that ranks 101st nationally. The absence of so much defensive firepower, however, puts more pressure on Sarkisian's offense, which has failed to deliver a consistent product halfway through the season. He promised to evaluate everything in his program following the loss to the Gators, but he has yet to name a single change in the starting lineup or mention exactly what this team will do differently after going 1-2 in SEC play. He was adamant that he needs to see more out of his beleaguered quarterback, Arch Manning, who said the same things himself. He did say he likes Manning's mental approach all week. How did he phrase it? "I would use the word edgy," Sarkisian said to describe Manning's attitude. "And I like it. He's edgy right now." Someone texted Sarkisian this week and told him that Texas has "lost the aw-shucks kid and created something else." Sarkisian said everyone - reporters, fan base, social media, coaches - helped create the out-of-control expectations for Manning, whose record as a starter is 16-5, and the junior quarterback has evolved through that process. "At some point, he's got to fight back, and the best way for him to fight back is going out and playing really good football with his teammates," Sarkisian said. "He's edgy right now, and honestly I appreciate that about him. I'm looking forward to watching him compete Saturday night." Asked about trying to institute effective change in less than a week, Sarkisian said, "That's a bit difficult to overhaul. I think when you use the word overhaul, that's probably an offseason term in any aspect of your program. Like, overhaul is a really big word. Can you make adjustments? Sure you can. But just to overhaul, I know Coach (Darrell) Royal would love this, but we can't come out in the wishbone Saturday night. That's tough to do in a six-day span." And it especially doesn't make sense from a team-running perspective, unless Golden State would also be sending Boston loads of draft capital. Even then, the Celtics clearly don't want to rebuild, nor should they, so they're going to try and figure things out with Tatum as the focal point this season. item.title: Rece Davis has a new No. 1 for a third straight week entering Week 8
item.description: ESPN "College GameDay" college football analyst Rece Davis saw his No. 1 ranked team lose for a third consecutive week. Davis is a voter the AP Poll. The Georgia Bulldogs were his previous No. 1, but the Bulldogs lost to Auburn Tigers and are no longer in his top five college football teams. The BYU Cougars are Davis' new No. 1 team after a chaotic Week 7 that featured five of the nation's top eight teams lose. BYU beat Notre Dame at home to earn Davis' top ranking. After BYU, Davis ranks undefeated Miami second. Then he has Ohio State at No. 3, Notre Dame at No. 4 and Indiana at No. 5. Tennessee, Texas Tech and Houston all joined Davis' top 10 rankings with Alabama, Texas and Utah all moving out. Both Alabama and Texas suffered their second loss of the season in Week 7. Week 8 does not have as many top matchups as Week 7, but it still shapes up as a key week with many teams facing potential elimination from the College Football Playoff picture. David Moyes needs another centre-forward, yet the club must find a solution without committing substantial funds to the wrong profile. However, their summer business left a significant gap in attack, with Beto joining Fiorentina for a reported £14.6m and a proposed move for Folarin Balogun collapsing before the deadline. Thierno Barry consequently carries much of the responsibility up front. item.title: Kylian Mbappé tried to give his MOTM award to Real Madrid teammate after win over RB Leipzig
item.description: Kylian Mbappé tried to give his MOTM award to Real Madrid teammate after win over RB Leipzig Photos stemming from the aftermath of Real Madrid’s victory over RB Leipzig on Wednesday night have brought smiles to the faces of Blancos fans the world over. This comes after Kylian Mbappé was spotted handing his Man of the Match trophy to a fellow member of José Mourinho’s squad. Real Madrid were of course back in action yesterday evening, welcoming German outfit RB Leipzig to Spain’s capital for a League Phase clash in the Champions League. When all was said and done, Los Merengues emerged on the right side of a 4-1 result. The aforementioned Kylian Mbappé was responsible for both a goal and an assist across the 90 minutes, culminating in the Frenchman securing the official UEFA Man of the Match prize. Post-match, however, the ex-PSG man attempted to hand his trophy to attacking partner-in-crime Yan Diomandé. After winger Diomandé emerged from the bench to notch a stunning goal as well as an assist of his own, Mbappé lightheartedly showcased his appreciation for his young teammate courtesy of the gesture showcased below: Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Mitchell Robinson breaks down injury scare, playing Knicks for 1st time
item.description: BOSTON — Mitchell Robinson took a tough fall midway through the first half against the Pistons on Tuesday. He looked like he tweaked his left ankle, hobbling back to the Celtics bench to get looked at by trainers. By the end of the timeout, Robinson was fine and stayed in the game. So, early injury scare avoided. “You tweak an ankle you’re going to feel a little bit here and there,” Robinson said ahead of Celtics practice Thursday. “But (expletive) happens. I just feel like I was playing fast.” Robinson took ownership after a slow Celtics debut where he only racked up one offensive rebound. He didn’t play up to his standards, he said, finishing with four points, three rebounds and two blocks in 18 minutes. He prides himself on his defense and rebounding, but he wasn’t effective enough on both ends. Now, Robinson gets another test: Facing his former team. The defending champion Knicks visit TD Garden at 7 p.m. Friday. It’s the first time Robinson will play New York since signing with the Celtics in free agency. With the Knicks being cost-conscious — looking at the Karl-Anthony Towns negotiations — they couldn’t afford to keep Robinson this summer. Robinson didn’t sound too emotional about the game, though. “It don’t really matter that much,” Robinson said. “It’s more so just trying to bounce back from what happened two nights ago. At the end of the day, basketball is a business and we gotta play the teams like you play the other teams.” Robinson experienced plenty of highs with the Knicks, including winning the 2026 NBA championship with them. He was in New York for eight years, so Robinson got to be part of the ascension to the mountaintop. He was a bench piece for the Knicks who brought plenty of physicality and offensive rebounding to the court. Detroit did a good job limiting Boston’s centers on those offensive rebounding chances throughout the night. But Robinson stressed he’s just looking to bounce back after he thought it was a lackluster debut. “He’s a very important piece to what we do,” C’s coach Joe Mazzulla said. “So the standard is a little bit higher and the expectation is a little bit higher. item.description: Marc DesRosiers-Imagn Senators make hugely discouraging Linus Ullmark injury move appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Ottawa Senators are off to a terrific start in 2026-27, going 7-3-0 through their first 10 games. The latest exclamation point was Wednesday night’s 5-1 drubbing of Brady Tkachuk and the Florida Panthers on home ice, a contest with no shortage of fireworks. But things are going to get considerably more difficult without star goaltender Linus Ullmark , who exited the victory with a lower-body injury. He was placed on injured reserve Thursday, ruling him out for at least seven days from the injury. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “That’s at least three games and likely more,” longtime Senators reporter Bruce Garrioch reported shortly after the announcement. Ullmark made a save on a hard shot from former teammate Tkachuk in the third period before hunching over in pain, prompting officials to stop play. The Sens have placed goaltender Linus Ullmark on injured reserve and he will be out at least a week 🤕 Ullmark appeared to tweak something during a routine save in the 3rd period of last night's game and needed assistance getting off the ice. pic.twitter.com/L2Ga3aThDh — Gino Hard (@GinoHard_) October 22, 2026 Head coach Travis Green said the Swede is dealing with a lower-body strain and would undergo further evaluation Thursday. No recovery timeline has been announced. Entering Wednesday’s contest, Ullmark had posted a 6-1-0 record with a sparkling 1.33 goals-against average and .945 save percentage. Samuel Ersson played the final 16:35, stopping the only shot he faced. He figures to handle the starting duties until Ullmark is ready to return. Ullmark also exited a game against the Boston Bruins earlier this month following a collision with JJ Peterka. It’s unclear whether the two injuries are related. In a corresponding move, the Senators recalled Jonas Johansson from the American Hockey League’s Belleville Senators. The 31-year-old most recently played for the Tampa Bay Lightning, recording 11 wins in 25 appearances last season while backing up Andrei Vasilevskiy. Johansson could get a look during Ullmark’s absence, particularly with Ersson having lost both of his starts while conceding 11 goals to the Detroit Red Wings and St. Louis Blues. For an Ottawa team looking to build on its strong start, replacing Ullmark’s excellent early production will be a significant test. The Senators are back in action against Macklin Celebrini and the visiting San Jose Sharks on Thursday night, with Ersson expected to start the cross-conference matchup. item.title: Panthers Set to Be Without Jaelan Phillips Against Buccaneers After Hamstring Injury
item.description: Photo by: Bob Donnan The Carolina Panthers are expected to be without one of their most important defensive players this Sunday, as outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips is unlikely to play against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers because of a hamstring injury. Panthers head coach Dave Canales delivered the update Wednesday after Phillips missed the team’s walkthrough. The injury is particularly concerning because the pass rusher aggravated the same hamstring problem during Carolina’s victory over the Philadelphia Eagles last Sunday. Phillips managed to return to that game and finish the contest, but the Panthers are now preparing to move forward without him for their upcoming divisional matchup. With a demanding stretch of the schedule ahead, Carolina will need its defensive front to step up. Phillips’ Injury Creates a Defensive Challenge Phillips originally sustained the hamstring injury during Carolina’s Week 4 victory over the Detroit Lions. After receiving additional time to recover during the team’s bye week, he returned against Philadelphia but experienced another setback. Canales indicated that the team needs to be careful with the injury rather than risk making the situation worse by rushing Phillips back onto the field. The outside linebacker has been one of Carolina’s most disruptive defenders this season, recording a team-leading 18 quarterback pressures entering the matchup. His ability to generate pressure without requiring extra blitzers has been an important part of the Panthers’ defensive approach. Losing that production against Tampa Bay could make life more difficult for Carolina’s defense, particularly against a Buccaneers offense capable of taking advantage of additional time in the pocket. Panthers Need Others to Step Up With Phillips expected to miss Sunday’s game, Carolina will need contributions from the rest of its outside linebacker group. Patrick Jones II, Princely Umanmielen and Trevis Gipson could all play important roles in helping replace Phillips’ production. The Panthers could also turn to practice-squad linebacker Nick Hampton for additional depth. Generating pressure will be especially important against Tampa Bay. If Carolina cannot consistently disrupt the quarterback, the Buccaneers could find opportunities to sustain drives and put points on the board. Could Phillips Miss More Time? The Panthers have not announced a firm timetable for Phillips’ return. Canales acknowledged that the team must consider the bigger picture rather than focus exclusively on getting him back for one game. Carolina also faces a short turnaround before playing Green Bay next Thursday, making his recovery timeline worth monitoring. For now, the priority is getting Phillips healthy. His absence is a significant setback for the Panthers, but protecting his long-term availability could prove more important than rushing him back too soon.

item.title: Nick Martinez to start game one of the 2026 World Series
item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 17: Nick Martinez #28 of the Tampa Bay Rays throws a pitch during the first inning against the Cleveland Guardians in game four of the American League Championship Series at Progressive Field on October 17, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last offseason, Nick Martinez was seeking an opportunity with a team that would allow him be a starting pitcher. Now, he is starting the first game of the World Series for the Tampa Bay Rays as they take on the Milwaukee Brewers. Tampa Bay signed Martinez just prior to Spring Training, Martinez was excited by the prospect of getting the chance to showcase himself as a full-time starting pitcher, “I’ve always believed that I can be a starter from beginning to end.” Over the course of the regular season, the now 36-year old Martinez more than proved himself as he delivered an All-Star season for Tampa Bay. Over the course of 31 starts, Martinez compiled a 3.10 ERA | 3.96 FIP with a 15.1 K% and league leading 3.6 BB% over a career high 180 innings pitched. Thus far in the postseason, Martinez has only appeared in two games, allowing three runs on seven hits over 9 IP. First pitch is slated a little after 8:00pm Friday night

item.title: Eagles sign former Giants draft pick to practice squad, re-sign two other players
item.description: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images | Getty Images A day after bringing in former first-round draft pick Evan Neal for a tryout, the Eagles are signing the former New York Giants offensive lineman to the practice squad, according to multiple reports. The team also announced re-signing RB Jaydon Blue and LB Anfernee Orji to the practice squad, and made the E.J. Jenkins waiving official . We have signed RB Jaydon Blue, G Evan Neal, and LB Anfernee Orji to the practice squad. We have also waived TE E.J. Jenkins. pic.twitter.com/8ngJbpakmw — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 22, 2026 As Brandon Lee Gowton wrote on Wednesday about adding Neal to the roster : “It doesn’t hurt for the Eagles to take a flyer on Neal, who turned 26 in September. Maybe there’s some untapped potential here for this coaching staff to maximize (you might feel better about that much if Jeff Stoutland was still around). More likely, he’s just not going to pan out in the NFL. But, hey, you never know.“ At this point the Eagles need depth up front and if there’s a shred of potential with Neal, it’s worth a shot to sign him. His versatility at multiple spots along the line is also a plus, since there’s still no continuity in Philly and players are still settling into new roles. The team still has several roster spots they can fill on the 53-man roster, and could sign some guys off the practice squad. Bottom line, with the growing list of injuries, this isn’t the last round of roster moves for the Eagles.

item.title: Former NY Giant joins the Philadelphia Eagles
item.description: ﻿Former New York Giants offensive lineman Evan Neal | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles have signed former New York Giants offensive lineman Evan Neal to their practice squad. Neal had recently been released from the Las Vegas Raiders practice squad, where he landed after being released in the Giants’ final cutdowns following the 2026 training camp. Neal, the 7th overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft, has been the biggest draft bust in recent memory for the Giants. He hasn’t played a regular season snap for the Giants since the 2024 season, when he filled in for Jermaine Eluemunor at right tackle. Eluemunor had originally been slated to play guard that year, but moved out to right tackle when Neal suffered an injury in camp. The Giants then converted Neal to guard in 2025, which was where he played in the 2026 off-season as well, but he never found his way to the field on game day. The Eagles’ decision to sign Neal comes as their offensive line is reshuffled by the retirement of RT Lane Johnson and the trade of OC Cam Jurgens. Philadelphia always seemed like a likely landing spot for Neal after he was released by the Giants. The Eagles have long prized size and power in their offensive linemen, both of which Neal has in spades. It remains to be seen if he’ll get the chance to compete for a starting job — or even be active on game days — as he attempts to salvage a once-promising career.

item.title: Shohei Ohtani Avoids Surgery, Expected to Return to Pitching in 2027
item.description: Photo by: Kirby Lee Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani received encouraging news heading into the offseason, as the two way sensation is not expected to need surgery and is projected to return to the mound during the 2027 MLB season. Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman confirmed Wednesday that surgery is not being considered for Ohtani’s left knee and right biceps injuries. After a frustrating end to the season, the organization expects the four-time MVP to recover with rest and be ready for the start of spring training. The announcement provides a major boost for Los Angeles as the team begins planning for next season and looks to get its biggest star back to full strength. Ohtani Expected to Return to Two Way Role Ohtani’s 2026 campaign was disrupted by injuries that eventually forced him to stop pitching. His last appearance on the mound came July 3, and repeated attempts to return were unsuccessful as he continued dealing with discomfort. Despite the setbacks, Ohtani remained one of baseball’s most dangerous hitters for much of the season. He finished with 30 home runs and an .889 OPS, while also posting an impressive 1.79 ERA across 14 starts and 85⅔ innings. Those numbers demonstrate just how valuable Ohtani can be when he contributes both offensively and on the mound. His ability to serve as an elite hitter and starting pitcher makes him one of the most unique players in baseball history. Friedman made it clear that the Dodgers are excited about getting Ohtani back to pitching, although the organization still needs to determine how to manage his workload. Dodgers Must Protect Their Superstar The biggest challenge heading into 2027 will be keeping Ohtani healthy throughout a full season. The Dodgers want him contributing as both a hitter and pitcher without allowing the demands of his workload to affect his availability late in the year. One possibility is to ease Ohtani back into pitching rather than immediately giving him a full workload at the beginning of the season. The team has not finalized a plan, and discussions will continue throughout the offseason. Ohtani has also expressed his desire to return to his two-way role after missing the final months of the season as a pitcher. A Major Boost for Los Angeles Avoiding surgery gives Ohtani a clearer path toward recovery and gives the Dodgers reason to be optimistic about 2027. After an injury filled season and an early postseason exit, Los Angeles will be looking for a bounce-back campaign. Having Ohtani healthy and pitching again could make a significant difference as the Dodgers pursue another championship. While his exact workload remains uncertain, the expectation is clear: Ohtani is preparing to return to the mound next season.

item.title: Five NFL teams play three consecutive primetime games this season; zero did so last year. Mike Florio thinks he knows why
item.description: Credit: PFT Live On Thursday’s episode of PFT Live , NBC Sports NFL insider Mike Florio soft launched a theory that could have legs . Florio, who’s as discerning an NFL observer as just about anyone in sports media, noticed that the Chicago Bears are about to begin a streak of three consecutive primetime games when they kickoff Week 7 on Thursday Night Football against the New England Patriots. The Bears (Weeks 7-9) join the Dallas Cowboys (Weeks 5-7), Seattle Seahawks (Weeks 6-8), Los Angeles Rams (Weeks 1-3), and the Atlanta Falcons (Weeks 3-5) as teams that will have streaks of at least three consecutive primetime affairs this season. That’s five NFL teams playing in three consecutive primetime games this season. The number of teams that did so last year? Zero. That struck Florio as quite unusual. Perhaps other than the Kansas City Chiefs or the New England Patriots at the peak of their dynastic powers, it’s difficult to think of instances where a single team ever played in three consecutive primetime games. To have five such teams in a single season is definitely bizarre. Florio thinks there’s a reason for this. If the NFL ever wanted to introduce a regular package of midweek games on Tuesday or Wednesday night, those games would necessarily require teams to feature in primetime, standalone windows in consecutive weeks. For instance, a team could play Thursday night one week, then Wednesday the following week, and Tuesday after that. That’d give teams the requisite amount of rest between games, while still allowing the NFL to take advantage of these open midweek windows. It stands to reason that the NFL would want to test how audiences react to seeing the same teams in primetime during three consecutive weeks. Would fans lose interest? Or conversely, would fans become more interested in seeing the same teams repeatedly? And how would the teams themselves handle playing three straight night games? These are all key data points the NFL would like to have if they were ever to seriously consider creating a Wednesday or a Tuesday package. The league claimed last month that the consecutive primetime games were simply a quirk in this year’s schedule. “[T]his happens a few times a year and was not intentional, but rather a function of how the overall 272-game schedule works out,” a league spokesperson told Forbes . “It’s a combination of opponents, stadium availability, viewership predictions, network requests, etc.” NFL executives have repeatedly insisted the league will tread lightly on adding any more midweek contests to the schedule. Ratings data for the first Wednesday game this season, the season opener featuring the Seahawks and Patriots, were already soft compared to the normal Thursday opener . The next Wednesday data point will come on Thanksgiving Eve, when the Packers play the Rams. The NFL, to its credit, is always quite diligent in making these types of schedule changes, at least in terms of the league’s sensitivity to viewership trends

item.title: MLB Network analysts pick Milwaukee Brewers Brice Turang as World Series MVP
item.description: Brice Turang has emerged as a potential World Series MVP candidate after the Milwaukee Brewers swept the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS to reach the Fall Classic for the first time since 1982. Jake Bauers claimed NLCS MVP honors following an impressive series, but could Turang take home the Fall Classic award? In a video posted by MLB Network, several pundits and personalities shared their MVP picks, and Turang’s name came up twice. Who are you picking to win the 2026 World Series MVP? pic.twitter.com/6iAq5cShKd — MLB Network (@MLBNetwork) October 21, 2026 Matt Vasgersian, the first person featured in the video, picked Turang for World Series MVP while predicting the Brewers to win the championship. He expects the second baseman to steal a couple of bases and launch a few home runs during the series, putting him on track to claim the award. Mark DeRosa also named Turang as his Fall Classic MVP choice, backing Milwaukee to finish the series in six games. His pick may carry some personal influence, considering he coached Turang on Team USA during this year’s World Baseball Classic. Turang was not the only Brewer mentioned as a possible recipient, with William Contreras, Jake Bauers, Cooper Pratt, and starting pitcher Jacob Misiorowski also receiving consideration. Brice Turang with the Brewers Jul 12, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Milwaukee Brewers second baseman Brice Turang (2) circles the bases on a two run homer run against the Pittsburgh Pirates during the eighth inning at PNC Park. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Turang put together an impressive regular season, batting .268 while recording 21 homers and 100 RBIs. His production has dipped during Milwaukee’s postseason campaign, however, as he has flown under the radar on the Brewers’ path to the Fall Classic. He enters the Fall Classic with a .222 batting average, one home run, and two RBIs in the playoffs. Sep 4, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Milwaukee Brewers second baseman Brice Turang (2) bats against the Cincinnati Reds in the sixth inning at Great American Ball Park. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images Whether Turang can turn his postseason struggles around and deliver a Fall Classic performance worthy of the MVP award remains to be seen. For now, the two MLB Network personalities who backed him are hoping their prediction comes true. item.title: How many matches could Maignan miss after his red card for Milan at Bournemouth?
item.description: How many matches could Maignan miss after his red card for Milan at Bournemouth? Mike Maignan faces at least one game out in the Europa League after his first-half red card in Milan’s clash with Bournemouth. According to MilanNews24 , the goalkeeper will certainly miss Milan’s next European fixture, and the ban could be longer if UEFA rule the incident violent conduct. Maignan was sent off in the 27th minute when, during a Bournemouth corner, he pushed his hand into Tyler Adams’ face with no chance of playing the ball. After a VAR check, he was shown a straight red card, and Marcus Tavernier converted the resulting penalty to make it 2-0. Ruben Amorim was forced to sacrifice Omari Hutchinson to bring on young goalkeeper Lorenzo Torriani. BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 22: Tyler Adams of Bournemouth lies on the ground after a foul by Mike Maignan of AC Milan during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between AFC Bournemouth and AC Milan at Bournemouth Stadium on October 22, 2026 in Bournemouth, England. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) Maignan available for Serie A and the derby UEFA suspensions only apply to its own competitions, so Maignan will be available for Milan’s Serie A games. That includes Sunday’s trip to Udinese and the derby against Inter on 31 October. He will miss the visit of Ferencváros to San Siro on 5 November. If UEFA hands him a longer ban, he could also sit out the trip to Olympiacos on 26 November.

item.description: Jets finally get some good Breece Hall injury news on Week 7 practice report originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 2026 season for the New York Jets , all things considered, hasn't gone terribly. While only 2-4, the Jets have shown the ability to hang around with good teams, and that's even been the case as they deal with some injury issues. One of the biggest is the Breece Hall quad injury, which has kept him out for multiple weeks now. However, the Jets got some good news before Week 7 on Hall's injury. As the Jets announced in their Thursday Week 7 practice injury report, the star running back was finally upgraded at practice, as he was no longer a DNP but instead listed as a "limited" participant. Breece Hall upgraded at Jets practice in good news for Week 7 The Jets shared their Week 7 injury report for their game against the Miami Dolphins . Right in the middle of the injury report, Hall was seen with his quad injury as going from a "DNP" on Wednesday to a "LP" on Thursday. What that means is that, for the first time in a while, Hall got in a limited practice, which bodes well for his chances of suiting up on Sunday against the AFC East rival Dolphins. He isn't guaranteed to play this week, but getting in a limited practice, going from not participating on Wednesday to a limited participant on Thursday, is a sign that he's trending in the right direction. MORE : Cam Skattebo's lack of rushing attempts is a major cause for concern for Giants Braelon Allen has handled the RB workload in his absence and has been great. While Hall will take over the backfield going forward, Allen should still see some work. But for the Jets, the most important thing from this week's injury report is that Hall is back practicing and might actually be good to go for the first time since Week 3, when he ran for 32 yards against the Detroit Lions . Jets fans should keep a very close eye on the Friday injury report, because if Hall's a full participant, he's as good as playing. But even another limited participation would indicate his work Thursday went well, and he'd have a chance to go in Week 7. item.title: Mike Washington Jr. not spotted during Las Vegas Raiders’ Thursday practice ahead of Week 7 Los Angeles Rams’ matchup
item.description: (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders running back Mike Washington Jr. was absent during the media viewing portion of Thursday’s practice ahead of the Week 7 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams , according to The Athletic’s Sam Warren . Mike Washington Jr. is not here with the Raiders RB group to start practice. He was limited yesterday with foot and back injuries. pic.twitter.com/O2e9yBP08p — Sam Warren (@samwarren83) October 22, 2026 Washington was listed as a limited participant with foot and back injuries during Wednesday’s session. The Raiders haven’t released Thursday’s injury report at the time of writing — Silver and Black Pride will update this story when they do — so the rookie running back hasn’t officially been declared a non-participant. However, if that is indeed the case, it appears he suffered a setback. The fourth-round pick has been the second back behind Ashton Jeanty through the first six games this season but had 10 touches for 50 yards from scrimmage last week against the Buffalo Bills, including nine rushes for 43 yards . His role is expected to increase as the Silver and Black figure out their rushing woes, ranking 30th in the NFL for total rushing yards and 31st in yards per attempt this fall. Obviously, that requires Washington to be healthy, though. Meanwhile, Jeanty, who has also battled injuries this year, wasn’t listed on Wednesday’s report and appears to be a full go. So, if Washington is available, the offense will still have its lead back, barring a significant change in the coming days. In other injury news, defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was spotted wearing a red, non-contact jersey on Thursday, per Warren . Hemingway suffered a concussion against the New England Patriots two weeks ago and missed last Sunday’s game against the Buffalo Bills. Wearing the red jersey suggests he’s limited in practice and one step closer to clearing the NFL’s concussion protocol. Warren also posted a video of tight end Brock Bowers warming up before Thursday’s practice. Bowers was limited Wednesday with hamstring and calf injuries, which is different from the knee injury that caused him to miss Weeks 1 and 2. That being said, he’s been limited on Wednesdays every week since returning to action. item.description: Le Bris backs Sunderland players after draw with Lech Poznan Régis Le Bris praised Sunderland’s response to draw 1-1 with Lech Poznan in the Europa League – and insisted recent Premier League defeats are no reason to doubt his players. The Black Cats have endured a difficult spell domestically, but Le Bris believes their performances in Europe have shown what his squad are capable of. “I think it was the right reaction,” Le Bris said. “We played well against Torreense and Alkmaar too. “Because we lost a few games in the Premier League, it doesn’t mean that the players or the team are weak. item.title: Lewis Hamilton “forced to stay a lot longer” in F1 amid African Grand Prix hopes
item.description: Motorsport photo It’s always an exciting time when Formula 1 plans a new race, but Ferrari ’s Lewis Hamilton is over the moon with the news that the championship is heading to Rwanda on a ten-year deal for an African Grand Prix. He’s so excited, in fact, that he’s hoping he can hold on and compete there when the time comes. The race is expected to take place in the early 2030s, which would put the seven-time F1 champion in his mid-40s. Sat beside Mercedes ’ Kimi Antonelli in the press conference ahead of this weekend’s United States Grand Prix, the Scuderia driver was asked whether anything had surprised him about the young driver’s first title fight. After praising Antonelli, he looked to his own future on the grid. “I’m looking forward to racing with him longer and we’ll see about, I mean, I’m now forced to have to stay a lot longer because we have a race in Africa and that’s been my dream, to be able to race in Africa.” Antonelli replied: “So you’ve got to come.” Hamilton added: “So, yeah, I mean, I have to keep fighting to try and stay fit if I can, if I can still punch out good results over the next year, we’ll keep it going.” It was not the first time Antonelli had urged him on. When Hamilton was first asked about the Rwanda race, the Mercedes driver interjected: “You got to do at least the first.” Stefano Domenicali at African GP announcement in Rwanda Stefano Domenicali at African GP announcement in Rwanda Hamilton has pushed for a grand prix in Africa for a long time, and said he had been heavily involved behind the scenes. “I’ve been advocating for a race in Africa for many, many, many years, and countless meetings with the stakeholders, so many meetings with Stefano [Domenicali, F1 CEO] at his office in London, but also race weekends, countless calls, what’s happening, where are we going, who are you meeting with, many meetings with different presidents from different countries, lots of phone calls with different presidents from different countries within Africa. “I think for me, it’s a place that deserves to have a grand prix. It’s more than just about one country. It’s about the continent in itself, and there’s so many beautiful countries within it, and the people are so lovely. The culture is so rich, and I think it’s important that we get to show that to the world, and we get to do that with our sport. “We get to go to all these different countries, and people see some of these countries they didn’t really know too much about, and all of a sudden, it’s on the screen, and kids are talking about it. They go to school talking about it, and so I’m really, really hopeful for that grand prix.” F1 has not raced in Africa since the 1993 South African Grand Prix at Kyalami. If you’re a Hamilton fan, you’ll be crossing your fingers he’s still there by the time Rwanda comes knocking. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Haiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisis
item.description: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US at Nu Stadium on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage Concacaf on Thursday announced it has approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg against the United States on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of the capital of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the US, had been booked for Kingston. The Grenadiers played their 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...

item.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
item.description: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now . He teaches at Marist University. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
